column3: A later generation inherits the Book yet chooses worldly gain, directly paralleling the failed succession in the focus.
One given divine signs abandons them and joins the misguided, illustrating departure from inherited guidance.
The preservation of believers' reward does not clarify neglected prayer, desires, or misguidance.
It explicitly couples denial with following desires, one of the focus ayah's central diagnoses.
The immediately preceding exemplary prophets prostrate and weep at revelation, the direct contrast to their successors.
Its designation of followers as misguided gives a limited parallel to the focus ayah's threatened ghayy.
Following God's pleasure is a broad positive contrast to following desires.

Punishment for forgetting the meeting with God and for one's deeds clarifies the logic of the announced consequence.

The statement about lying hearers does not clarify prayer or desire-following.

Seeking instruction in right guidance is a broad positive contrast to misguidance.
The unseen report about Mary's guardianship does not illuminate the focus.

The reward for untainted charity does not clarify the focus ayah.
The ruling about the Sacred Mosque and provision does not develop the warning.

The same-surah command to worship and persevere in worship is a direct corrective counterpart to neglecting prayer.

It warns against one who follows desire and turns another from the Hour, directly linking desire to ruin.
The command to enjoin one's family to prayer and persevere in it directly counters failed religious transmission.
It forbids obeying one whose heart neglects God's remembrance and follows desire, a very close formulation.
It explicitly forbids following desire because it leads away from God's path.
Taking one's desire as a god gives an acute account of the focus ayah's corrupt allegiance.
It condemns following conjecture and what souls desire rather than the guidance that has come.
The questioning of the people of Hell introduces a direct account of the consequences of religious failure.

Their constancy in prayer sharply contrasts with the focus ayah's abandonment of it.
The summons to Friday prayer requires leaving worldly trade, directly opposing worldly desire's priority over prayer.
Prayer is said to restrain indecency and wrongdoing, clarifying the moral loss entailed by abandoning it.
Taking personal desire as a god gives a direct conceptual parallel to following shahawat as guidance.
Prayer is prescribed at appointed times, clarifying the obligation that the later generation fails to maintain.
The hypocrites rise for prayer lazily, a concrete mode of religious neglect.
Their prayer is performed only reluctantly, adding another concrete form of compromised observance.
Abraham's prayer that his descendants establish prayer makes successful intergenerational transmission explicit.
The prophets are inspired to do good, establish prayer, and give alms, countering the focus ayah's later decline.
Those established in the land establish prayer and command right, linking authority to faithful practice.
Luqman commands his son to establish prayer and endure hardship, a family-transmission countermodel.
The devoted servant praying by night contrasts sustained worship with abandonment of prayer.
Remembering God's name and praying provides a concise positive alternative to heedless desire-following.
The attempted prohibition of a servant at prayer highlights prayer as a central contested act of devotion.
Sincere worship, prayer, and almsgiving define upright religion, contrasting the focus ayah's collapse.
The command to guard prayers directly counters the focus ayah's loss of prayer.
Seeking the Hereafter with faithful effort contrasts orienting one's life around worldly shahawat.
Turning away from the Merciful's remembrance brings a satanic companion, explaining a path into misguidance.
